item.title: Rust for Web Backends in 2026: Axum vs Actix vs Rocket
item.description: I spent the last few months building three small but real backends — a webhook relay, an internal admin API, and a rate-limited proxy — each in a different Rust web framework, on purpose. Not a toy benchmark, actual services with auth, database pools, and traffic. The goal was simple: figure out which Rust web framework I’d actually reach for by default in 2026, and which ones only make sense in specific situations.

item.title: eBPF in 2026: The Linux Superpower Every Backend Developer Should Understand
item.description: A few months back I had a Node service that was randomly stalling for a couple hundred milliseconds every few minutes. No exceptions, no error logs, nothing in the APM dashboard worth screenshotting. Application-level tracing was useless because the problem wasn’t in the application — it was somewhere between the syscall layer and the disk. The tool that actually cracked it open wasn’t a new logging library or a fancier metrics agent.

item.title: Linux Kernel 7.0 Didn't Halve PostgreSQL Throughput — Here's What Actually Happened
item.description: A headline went around a few weeks ago claiming Linux Kernel 7.0 “halved PostgreSQL throughput.” If you run any kind of production database on Linux, that’s the kind of sentence that ruins your afternoon. I dug into it because I was about to upgrade a few boxes myself, and the real story is a lot less scary than the headline. It’s also a much better story if you actually care about where Linux is heading, because the headline buried the genuinely interesting part — stable Rust support landing in the kernel — under a benchmark scare that mostly wasn’t about the kernel at all.

item.title: C++ vs Rust vs Go in 2026: Which One Should You Actually Learn?
item.description: Every few months someone asks me the same question: “should I learn Rust or just stick with C++?” Lately Go gets thrown into that question too. I’ve written a lot of C++, poked at Rust, and shipped small things in Go — so here’s my honest 2026 take, backed by what’s actually happening in the ecosystem right now, not vibes. Why this comparison actually matters in 2026 This isn’t an academic exercise.
